questions.prompt: Explain the difference between setNeedsLayout() and layoutIfNeeded() in UIKit. Answer in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that setNeedsLayout is asynchronous and marks the view dirty for the next run loop pass
Explains that layoutIfNeeded is synchronous and forces immediate layout execution if the dirty flag is set

questions.modelAnswer: In UIKit, setNeedsLayout() is an asynchronous method. It flags a view as dirty and schedules a layout pass on the next run loop turn. It returns immediately and allows multiple layout requests to coalesce. In contrast, layoutIfNeeded() is synchronous; if the view is marked dirty, it immediately calls layoutSubviews() without waiting. This makes layoutIfNeeded() essential for animating Auto Layout changes inside animation blocks.

questions.prompt: Why should you never call layoutSubviews() directly in your custom view code? Answer in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that layoutSubviews is a system callback managed by the UIKit layout engine
Explains to call setNeedsLayout to request layout or layoutIfNeeded to force immediate execution

questions.modelAnswer: You should never invoke `layoutSubviews()` directly because it is a system-level lifecycle callback managed by the UIKit layout engine. Calling it manually bypasses the run loop coalescing mechanism and does not properly update dirty ancestor or descendant views. Instead, call `setNeedsLayout()` to request an asynchronous pass or `layoutIfNeeded()` when an immediate synchronous update is required.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of intrinsicContentSize and how do you inform the layout system when it changes? Answer in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that intrinsicContentSize defines a view natural size based on its contents
Explains that calling invalidateIntrinsicContentSize tells Auto Layout to recalculate constraints

questions.modelAnswer: The `intrinsicContentSize` property defines the natural, intrinsic dimensions of a view derived from its content, such as text length or image dimensions. This allows Auto Layout to measure and position views without requiring explicit width or height constraints. Whenever content changes and alters these natural dimensions, you must call `invalidateIntrinsicContentSize()` so the layout engine knows to recalculate parent and sibling constraints.

questions.prompt: Explain how to properly animate an Auto Layout constraint change using UIView.animate. Answer in 2 to 5 sentences.
questions.lessonSection: How to answer in the interview

rubric.criterion: Explains updating the constraint constant property
Explains calling layoutIfNeeded on the container view inside the UIView.animate block

questions.modelAnswer: To animate a constraint change, you first update the constraint constant property on the main thread. Next, inside the UIView.animate block, you call layoutIfNeeded() on the container view. Calling layoutIfNeeded() inside the animation closure forces UIKit to recalculate subview frames immediately. Core Animation then smoothly interpolates the geometric changes.

questions.prompt: Why is calling super.layoutSubviews() mandatory when overriding layoutSubviews in a custom view? Answer in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that super.layoutSubviews executes the Auto Layout engine subview positioning pass
Explains that omitting super.layoutSubviews prevents subviews from receiving their calculated frames

questions.modelAnswer: Calling `super.layoutSubviews()` is mandatory because it invokes the underlying Auto Layout engine pass to compute and apply frames to all managed subviews. If you omit the `super` call, constraint equations will not resolve into concrete subview geometries, leaving subviews misplaced or with zero frames. Always call `super.layoutSubviews()` at the beginning of your custom implementation before performing additional manual adjustments.
